design.cohort: Frozen initial 27 entities; all 25 accepted DESI + PS1 spectra; 2 unavailable retained with reasons
design.objective: Minimum continuous supremum of absolute fractional change across the entire retained spectral range
design.error_policy: Swan published PS1 errors already contain their 0.01 mag quadrature floor. No additional floor is added here. The saved baseline used max(quoted error, 0.02 mag); this new experiment varies measured-band intervals explicitly.
design.box_definition: For each used band, observed_mag - k*quoted_error <= synthetic_mag <= observed_mag + k*quoted_error; k=0 fixes the catalogue central values
design.XYZ_policy: Each integrated XYZ component is constrained above 1e-8 of its positive baseline value
design.colour_sets: green_closed = G>=R and G>=B; non_green = (G<=R) or (G<=B), solved as two LPs. Ties belong to both sets; strict green dominance is not certified by a boundary witness.
design.norm_computation: 8 A initial constraint grid plus knots; iterative inclusion of all analytic derivative roots and knots; final continuous witness supremum checked against LP objective
design.scope: Observed colour at Earth; fixed signed spectral samples after the existing finite/IVAR and narrow sky masks; same PS1 survey; no extinction correction, new noise draw or inter-survey independence assumption
limitations: Existence/minimum in chosen spline spaces, not inferred calibration error, confidence, probability or atmosphere-model perturbation
Error boxes are neither a joint confidence region nor a covariance model; PS1 shared errors and non-simultaneity are not inferred
Adding z in griz uses it for fitting. It must no longer be described as held out in that scenario
Results condition on the frozen selected spectra. Pixel covariance, bit masks absent from MWDD arrays and unknown systematics remain
Spacing choices are sensitivity scenarios, not measured instrumental correlation lengths
Numerical LP/extrema agreement is not a formal interval-arithmetic optimality certificate
Failure with t<=0.95 is infeasibility within this bounded model, not proof that a real star cannot have a given colour
